Where this approach may not be technically achievable in some situations, e.g. due to transport limitations, then on-site stick-build installations can still be utilized. 4.10.2 CIVIL WORKS Civil works including ground work to support equipment receipt will be the first step in the development of the site. Key activities will include:  Preparation of a construction barge berthing location to the north of the site,  Installation of a temporary construction bridge to cross the existing LPG pipeline safely. Elevated civil ground works on either side of the pipeline will allow a Bailey type bridge to be laid out and positioned across the pipe.  Paving the roads on site as per the final site plan, to be utilized during construction. Including the main site access from Pendola Point Road.  Preparation of area in the future expansion area on the east side of the site to lay out procurement materials / equipment on arrival. The parcel currently ranges in elevation from 8.1 feet at the southwest corner to 17.6 feet in the eastern half. Elevations refer to the North American Datum of 1988 (NAVD88). Therefore, it must be filled as necessary and graded to make it level for the installation of equipment and buildings, but with adequate sloping towards planned and installed drainage points (between 0.5% and 1.0% slope). Any fill used will be free of any deleterious material, well-drained and compacted to a minimum of 85% density in accordance with ASTM 01557-02. After it is filled and graded for use as the T-RICH facility, it is projected to be 13.5 feet throughout the center drainage basin to 14.5 feet near the perimeter. Page94 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version The only known structure on the site are three wood poles supporting power lines to a floodlight. These are planned to be removed prior to grading. Any potential underground structures will be identified during thorough site surveys in future phases of the project. During construction a silt fence will be installed around the perimeter of the site to prevent sediment from being carried beyond the perimeter with storm water or other means until permanent surfaces (e.g. asphalt, gravel) and drainage systems are installed. The silt fence will be a minimum of 16 inches above ground and 8 inches below ground. It will be supported by wood posts driven into the ground no more than 6 feet apart. Additionally, as the site’s drainage system is constructed before the road is, AGIP (at grade inlet protection) is used around/over the FDOT Type C & D catch basins to ensure that debris from construction does not enter the drainage system.
